rationale: One critical bug found: formatTimezoneLabel does not guard against invalid/unrecognized timezone strings. When luxon cannot resolve a zone, .offset returns NaN, and formatUtcOffset(NaN) produces the literal string 'UTC-NaN:NaN' in the rendered label — confirmed by both review lenses with runtime verification. Any stored legacy or non-IANA timezone value (Windows IDs, typos, old database rows) will show corrupted text in DataSourceDetails. Two findings deferred: (1) module-level cache freezes DST offsets at first call — explicitly accepted as a known limitation in the plan; (2) displayed offset reflects current time rather than schedule-execution time — inherent limitation of showing a static UTC offset for DST-observing timezones. findings.problem: formatTimezoneLabel does not validate the timezone string — when luxon cannot resolve the zone, DateTime.now().setZone(tz).offset returns NaN, and formatUtcOffset(NaN) produces the literal string 'UTC-NaN:NaN'.
findings.impact: Any data source whose stored timezone is not recognized by luxon (legacy Windows IDs such as 'Eastern Standard Time', typos, or non-IANA values from the database) renders a corrupted label in DataSourceDetails (e.g. 'Eastern Standard Time (UTC-NaN:NaN)'). The sign is always '-' because NaN >= 0 evaluates to false.
findings.recommendation: Guard with luxon's isValid flag before formatting: const dt = DateTime.now().setZone(tz); const name = tz.replace(/_/g, ' '); return dt.isValid ? `${name} (${formatUtcOffset(dt.offset)})` : name; — this degrades gracefully to just the name for unrecognized values instead of showing corrupted text.
